$comment: What the Librarian reads from a model's reply, as every implementation of the Librarian must read it. Semiont's Librarian (apps/librarian) runs every case and fails on a difference; a Librarian in another language runs the same file. There are two readers, and a case's `reader` says which it is of. `reply` is the model's reply, whole. THE READER OF `scores` reads the reply to a score prompt (specs/src/librarian/prompt-cases.json), which listed `candidates` candidates, numbered from 1. `scores` is what is read: each item is the number of a `candidate`, as the reply writes it and as the prompt numbered it, and the `score` read for it. A candidate that is not in `scores` has no score read. The rule: the white space at the two ends of the reply is dropped, and what is left is read a line at a time, the lines parted by a line feed. A line is read when it starts with a number written in the digits 0 to 9, then a full stop, then any white space or none, then a score written in digits and full stops. What follows the score on its line is not read. The line gives a score when its number is one of the candidates', 1 to `candidates`, and its score is a number from 0 to 1, both ends included. Every other line gives nothing, and is no error. Where two lines give a score for one candidate, the later is the one read. THE READER OF `suggestions` reads the reply to a reference-suggestions prompt. `suggestions` is the list read. The empty reply answers none, and its `suggestions` is `null`. The rule: the reply is read a line at a time, the lines parted by a line feed. A bullet that starts a line, a hyphen, an asterisk or a round bullet (U+2022), is dropped with the white space after it, and so is the white space at the two ends of the line. A line with nothing left is dropped. The first three lines left are the suggestions. Add a case here before changing an implementation.

cases.why: each line that gives a candidate's number and a score is read
a line that is not a number and a score gives nothing, and the lines around it are read
cases.reply:
Here are my scores:
1. 0.8
The second is not relevant.
3. 0.4

cases.why: a line that scores fewer candidates than were listed leaves the others unread
a number past the last candidate gives nothing
the number 0 is before the first candidate, and gives nothing
a score above 1 gives nothing
a score with a minus sign is not written in digits and full stops: its line gives nothing
a score written in words gives nothing
a score of full stops alone is no number, and gives nothing
the scores 0 and 1 are both read, however they are written
the white space at the two ends of the reply is dropped before its lines are read
the white space between the full stop and the score may be several spaces, a tab, or none
what follows the score on its line is not read
lines that end with a carriage return and a line feed are read as the others are
where two lines score one candidate, the later is read
a number written in other digits than 0 to 9 is not read
white space is dropped at the ends of the reply and not of each line: a line inside the reply that starts with a space does not start with a number, and gives nothing
the empty reply gives no scores
a reply of white space alone gives no scores
three plain lines are three suggestions
cases.reply:
Read the treaty of 1804
Compare the Sauk and Meskwaki accounts
Map the crossing at Yellow Banks
suggestions: Compare the Sauk and Meskwaki accounts
Map the crossing at Yellow Banks

cases.why: a hyphen at the start of a line, and the space after it, are dropped
cases.reply:
- Read the treaty
- Compare the accounts
- Map the crossing

cases.why: an asterisk at the start of a line is dropped the same way
cases.reply:
* Read the treaty
* Compare the accounts
* Map the crossing

cases.why: a round bullet at the start of a line is dropped the same way
cases.reply:
• Read the treaty
• Compare the accounts
• Map the crossing

cases.why: a bullet is dropped whether no space, several spaces or a tab follow it
cases.reply:
-Read the treaty
*   Compare the accounts
•	Map the crossing

cases.why: a hyphen inside a line stays

- Read the pre-war treaty
Compare the accounts - both of them
suggestions: Compare the accounts - both of them

cases.why: the white space at the two ends of a line is dropped
cases.reply:
Read the treaty  
	Compare the accounts	
- Map the crossing

cases.why: empty lines are dropped

Compare the accounts

cases.why: a line of white space alone, and a bullet with nothing after it, are dropped

-

cases.why: of five suggestions the first three are read
dropped lines are not counted among the three
fewer than three lines are fewer than three suggestions

cases.why: the empty reply answers none
a reply that is not empty and has nothing on its lines answers an empty list, which is not none
